verdict_reason: 13 tiles found, from 3 photographers, and every frame that carries any locational evidence at all is Hoan Kiem Lake and its island temple. Independent hard proof from two different photographers: 3915909276 shows Thap Rua (the Turtle Tower) floodlit on its islet with its reflection, 3829368943 shows the same tower in daylight silhouette across the water, and 3933406885 shows the Dac Nguyet Lau gate of Den Ngoc Son - grey pillars, circular moon opening flanked by two gold dragons on a blue ground, glazed dragon and tiger relief panels, red The Huc bridge railing in the foreground. Four further frames (3834932797, 3834948237, 3835737268, 6545467201) are the red The Huc bridge on its red piles. The third photographer's temple interiors are unlabelled but sit in an unbroken upload run with their own The Huc bridge frame. Only one frame, a lakeside litter bin, carries no place evidence. The pin sits on its real subject.

photos.evidence: Dusk view across a wide sheet of still grey-green water; on the far side a low wooded shore and, mid-frame, the small tiered tower of Thap Rua standing on its own islet, with mid-rise city buildings behind the trees to the right.

Vermilion-red timber bridge on closely spaced red piles curving from the lakeside promenade to a wooded island, seen framed by overhanging branches; green lake water, city skyline low behind the far trees.
The same red bridge from lake level: red lattice balustrades on both sides, red piles standing in green water, a group of pedestrians in white on the deck, dense island foliage beyond.

Looking along the lakeshore under a big leaning tree: the red timber bridge on red piles crosses the frame left to right over green water, with a concrete lakeside kerb in the foreground and the far shore of the lake behind.

Stainless-steel public litter bin carrying a Salonpas/Hisamitsu advertisement panel (Vietnamese copy 'SAN PHAM CONG NGHE NHAT BAN'), a 'www.goldsungroup.com.vn' header, two flaps labelled 'RAC TU PHAN HUY'/'RAC KHONG PHAN HUY' and the bilingual line 'HAY BO RAC VAO THUNG / GIVE ME RUBBISH! THANK YOU!'. Proves Vietnam and a tourist-area park, but nothing behind it except dappled foliage and paving - no lake, no landmark, no street name.

Night shot of a curving lakeside promenade: pale patterned paving, a low kerb, white globe lamp standards, big spreading trees lit from below, and flat black-green water immediately to the right with lights reflected on the far shore. Reads as the Hoan Kiem lakeside walk; no legible text.

Thap Rua at night: the three-tier tower with arched openings on each level and a pyramidal top, floodlit orange-gold on its small islet, mirrored in the black water, with a line of distant street lights along the far shore.

The Dac Nguyet Lau gate of Den Ngoc Son: grey rendered gate with a central arch, above it a circular moon opening flanked by two gold dragons on a blue ground, a Han plaque under the tiled double roof, vertical Han couplet panels on the piers, and large glazed ceramic relief panels (blue-ground dragon at left, dragon at right) on the flanking walls; the red lattice railing of the The Huc bridge crosses the foreground.

Narrow stone-cobbled walkway squeezed between a low concrete kerb and a dark grey balustrade with square pierced panels and pier caps carrying large blue-and-white ceramic planters; a big old tree leans right across the path. Matches the balustraded terrace walk on the Ngoc Son island, and it is in the same photographer's run as the confirmed Dac Nguyet Lau frame.

The red timber bridge on red piles crossing green lake water to a tree-covered island, with pedestrians on the deck and the lakeside promenade and city trees on the far bank; framed by overhanging leaves.

Large dark bronze incense urn with cast dragon-scroll handles, full of yellow incense sticks, standing directly in front of tall red-lacquered plank doors with carved panels. No text. Tie to Ngoc Son is only that it sits in the same photographer's consecutive upload run as their The Huc bridge frame and the red doors match the Ngoc Son halls.

Temple hall interior: two tall gilded phoenix/crane figures flanking a red altar table set against a wall of red-and-gold pierced carved panels, a large bronze ceremonial drum on the floor, several big blue-and-white porcelain jars and a turquoise-glazed ceramic guardian lion at right. The gilded bird pair and the turquoise lion with blue-and-white jars match items recorded at Ngoc Son; no inscription legible here.

Close-up of a crowned, long-black-bearded deity statue in a red robe embroidered with gold dragons, seated in a dark red-lacquered niche with a ceremonial blade and flowers beside it. Consistent with the Van Xuong / Tran Hung Dao altars at Ngoc Son and inside the same upload run, but nothing written is visible.
